title: Quantized Enveloping Algebras and Quantum Serre Relations

items.title: Symmetrizable Cartan data for quantum groups
items.statement:
A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.
items.strategy: A definition item. The matrix has finite nonempty index set and the generalized Cartan conditions by [[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. A positive-integer symmetrizer can be chosen by [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. The pairings have the same row convention as [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]]; the independent simple roots give the direct-sum root lattice in [[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]. The minimal-realization proposition supplies independent root and coroot families by finite-dimensional linear algebra, with no use of arbitrary choice. The weight and coweight lattices and their integer pairing are part of the specified datum; they need not form a perfect pairing. Since $q$ is an indeterminate, $q_i$ and $q_i-q_i^{-1}$ are nonzero in $\mathbb Q(q)$. No fundamental weights are assumed, and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Quantum integers, factorials, Gaussian binomials and divided powers at $q_i$
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
items.strategy: A definition with two convention-conversion identities. From q_i^m−q_i^{-m}=q_i^{-(m-1)}(q_i^{2m}−1) and q_i−q_i^{-1}=q_i^{-1}(q_i^2−1), obtain [m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2}. Multiplication gives [m]_i!=q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}[m]_{q_i^2}!, and division of the three factorials yields the Gaussian shift exponent −r(m−r). For m=0 the empty-product convention handles the identities; for 0≤r≤m every denominator is a nonzero element of Q(q) because q is indeterminate and each d_i>0 ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]). Thus divided powers are defined, with the stated zero and unit cases. The symmetric q-integer and its factorial quotients are invariant under q_i↦q_i^{-1}. No choice is used.

items.title: The quantum Pascal recurrences, the Gauss product formula and Gaussian integrality
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.
items.strategy: Starting from the factorial quotient, derive the first Pascal recurrence using [m]_i=q_i^{-r}[m−r]_i+q_i^{m−r}[r]_i; derive the second from symmetry. For integrality, set G_{m,r}=q_i^{r(m−r)}C_{m,r}; the recurrence becomes G_{m,r}=G_{m−1,r}+q_i^{2(m−r)}G_{m−1,r−1}, and induction from G_{m,0}=G_{m,m}=1 gives G in Z[q_i²]. For the Gauss product, multiply the formula at N−1 by (1+q_i^{2(N−1)}z), compare coefficients using the first recurrence, and evaluate at z=−1 for the alternating identity. The cases N=0, r=0, r=m, and out-of-range r use the empty-product and zero conventions. Since q_i=q^{d_i} with d_i>0 and q indeterminate, evaluation of Z[t^{±1}] at t=q_i is injective; all identities therefore hold in the stated subrings. No choice is used.

items.title: The Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra by generators and relations
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).
items.strategy: Apply the tensor-algebra universal property to the generator symbols and quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by the toral, action, mixed, and both Serre families. The toral relations make K_{-h} the two-sided inverse of K_h. Each relation is homogeneous for deg(E_i)=alpha_i, deg(F_i)=−alpha_i, deg(K_h)=0, so the generated ideal is homogeneous and the quotient inherits the root-lattice direct-sum grading. Any assignment satisfying the relations extends to T, kills the ideal, and factors uniquely through U_q(g) by the quotient universal property. This definition asserts no nonvanishing or independence of the generators. No choice is used.

items.title: The quantum binomial expansion for $q$-commuting elements
items.statement:
Let $t$ be an indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$, and let $A$ be a unital associative $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra. For $N\ge0$ and $0\le r\le N$, set

$$B_{N,r}(t):=\frac{[N]_t!}{[r]_t![N-r]_t!},\qquad [m]_t:=1+t+\cdots+t^{m-1},\quad [m]_t!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_t,\quad [0]_t:=0,\quad [0]_t!:=1,$$

and set $B_{N,r}(t)=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>N$. If $x,y\in A$ satisfy $yx=txy$, then for every $N\ge0$,

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}B_{N,r}(t)x^ry^{N-r}.$$

For a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, any unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra can be viewed as a $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra via $t\mapsto q_i^2$. In that algebra, if $yx=q_i^2xy$, then

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-r)}\binom{N}{r}_i x^ry^{N-r},$$

using the symmetric Gaussian binomials of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. If instead $yx=t^{-1}xy$, the same expansion has coefficients $B_{N,r}(t^{-1})=t^{-r(N-r)}B_{N,r}(t)$.
items.strategy: Use the symmetric Pascal recurrence and the conversion C_{N,r}=q_i^{-r(N-r)}B_{N,r}(q_i²) to show that B_{N,r}(q_i²) obeys B_{N,r}=B_{N−1,r}+(q_i²)^{N−r}B_{N−1,r−1}; injectivity of t↦q_i² gives this recurrence for the generic asymmetric Gaussian quotient. Induct on N in (x+y)^N=(x+y)^{N−1}(x+y), using y^a x=t^a xy^a, to collect the coefficient of x^r y^{N−r}. The conversion then gives the q_i-symmetric coefficient. For t^{-1}, [k]_{t^{-1}}=t^{-(k−1)}[k]_t and the factorial quotient gives B_{N,r}(t^{-1})=t^{-r(N−r)}B_{N,r}(t). All expansions are finite; no ordinary commutative binomial theorem or choice is used.

items.title: Bialgebras, counits and antipodes over a commutative ring
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A **bialgebra over $R$** is a unital associative $R$-algebra $(A,m,\eta)$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) together with $R$-algebra homomorphisms $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_R A$ (the **coproduct**) and $\varepsilon:A\to R$ (the **counit**) such that $\Delta$ is coassociative and the counit axioms hold:

$$(\Delta\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)\Delta=(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\Delta)\Delta,\qquad (\varepsilon\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)\Delta=\operatorname{id}_A=(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta.$$

The counit equations use the canonical identifications $R\otimes_R A\cong A\cong A\otimes_R R$. The target $A\otimes_R A$ has the $R$-algebra structure of [[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]].

A **Hopf algebra over $R$** is a bialgebra $(A,m,\eta,\Delta,\varepsilon)$ together with an $R$-linear **antipode** $S:A\to A$ satisfying both convolution-inverse equations

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes S)\Delta,$$

where $(\eta\circ\varepsilon)(a)=\varepsilon(a)1_A$. We do not assume that $S$ is invertible, involutive or multiplicative. Throughout, $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are algebra homomorphisms, and the displayed order of the antipode factors is our convention.
items.strategy: A definition item. The target $A\otimes_R A$ is an $R$-algebra by [[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]], so that the algebra-homomorphism condition on $\Delta$ is meaningful. The counit equations use the canonical tensor-unit identifications; $\eta\circ\varepsilon$ is the $R$-linear map $a\mapsto\varepsilon(a)1_A$. All axioms are equalities of $R$-linear maps. The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of an antipode; uniqueness is [[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]. No choice is used.

items.title: Uniqueness of the antipode
items.statement: Let $(A,m,\eta,\Delta,\varepsilon)$ be a bialgebra over a commutative ring $R$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]) and let $S,S':A\to A$ be antipodes. Then $S=S'$. Thus a bialgebra admits at most one Hopf algebra structure with its fixed multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit. Every antipode also satisfies $S(1_A)=1_A$.
items.strategy: For R-linear maps f,g:A→A define f∗g=m(f⊗g)Δ. Coassociativity of Δ and associativity of m make ∗ associative. The two counit equations make e=η∘ε its two-sided unit. Both antipodes are two-sided convolution inverses to id_A; if S,S' are two such inverses, S=S∗e=S∗(id∗S')=(S∗id)∗S'=e∗S'=S'. Finally, Δ(1_A)=1_A⊗1_A and ε(1_A)=1_R, so evaluating either antipode equation at 1_A gives S(1_A)=1_A. No choice is used.

items.title: The Chevalley involution, the bar involution and the contravariant anti-involution preserve the defining ideal
items.statement: Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]. Define $\omega$ on generators by $E_i\mapsto-F_i$, $F_i\mapsto-E_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$, fixing $\mathbb Q(q)$; define $\psi$ by $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ with $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ on coefficients; and define $\tau$ by $E_i\mapsto F_i$, $F_i\mapsto E_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ with $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ on coefficients and reversed word order. Then all three preserve $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descend to involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear anti-involution. On Serre sums, $\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}$, $\psi$ fixes them, and $\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}$.
items.strategy: Extend the three generator assignments to the free algebra and check each relation family. The toral action images are relations at $-h$ up to scalar; the mixed commutator maps to the swapped $(j,i)$ relation (with sign for $\omega$), while the $q_i$-ratio is invariant under coefficient inversion. The Chevalley map contributes $m+1$ minus signs to the Serre sum; the anti-map reverses factors and reindexes $r\mapsto m-r$; the symmetric Gaussian coefficients are inversion-invariant. The original scaffold's claim that $\omega$ fixes the mixed commutator and its exponent for the $\psi$ toral image are corrected in the item.

items.title: The coproduct preserves the positive and negative quantum Serre ideals
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum, use the notation $q_i$, $K_h$ and $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put $m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$. Let $T^+$ and $T^-$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebras on the symbols $E_i,K_h$ and $F_i,K_h$, respectively. Let $R^+$ and $R^-$ be the two-sided ideals generated by $K_0-1$, $K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}$, and respectively $K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h$ or $K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h$. Define the toral-action algebras $B^+=T^+/R^+$ and $B^-=T^-/R^-$, and let $J^+$ and $J^-$ be their two-sided ideals generated by the images of the corresponding Drinfeld–Jimbo Serre elements.

The generator assignments

$$\Delta_+(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\qquad \Delta_+(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\qquad \Delta_-(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\qquad \Delta_-(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$$

define algebra homomorphisms $B^\pm\to B^\pm\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}B^\pm$. For every $i\ne j$, the Serre elements are quasiprimitive:

$$\Delta_+(\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}\otimes K_i^{-m_{ij}}K_j^{-1}+1\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij},\qquad \Delta_-(\mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}\otimes1+K_i^{m_{ij}}K_j\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}.$$

Consequently $\Delta_\pm(J^\pm)\subseteq J^\pm\otimes B^\pm+B^\pm\otimes J^\pm$. The canonical maps $B^\pm\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$ send the displayed coproducts of the Serre elements to zero in $U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak g)$; thus these formulas provide the Serre-family part of the check that the Drinfeld–Jimbo coproduct descends.
items.strategy: In the positive toral-action quotient, q-binomial-expand the two powers on either side of each coproduct term. Regroup by the left or right E_i-word; each mixed component is the alternating Gaussian sum with exponent N−1, while the two extreme components are the displayed Serre tensors. Obtain the negative formula by the generator-checked Chevalley coalgebra anti-symmetry, then extend from Serre generators to their two-sided ideals.

references.title: Richard Borcherds, Mark Haiman, Theo Johnson-Freyd, Nicolai Reshetikhin and Vera Serganova, Berkeley Lectures on Lie Groups and Quantum Groups

items.title: The Drinfeld-Jimbo formulas define a Hopf algebra
items.statement:
Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$
items.strategy: Extend the maps on the free algebra, verify the defining relations after mapping into U_q(g) tensor U_q(g), and use tensor right exactness to recover ker(pi tensor pi)=I_DJ tensor T+T tensor I_DJ. Check the counit and antipode on each relation family; the Serre antipode images are -K_i^m K_j Serre+ and -q_i^(2m)q_j^2 K_i^(-m)K_j^(-1) Serre-. Check coassociativity and the counit on generators, then extend the convolution identities to words by anti-multiplicativity and coproduct multiplicativity.

items.title: Positive, negative and toral quantum subalgebras and their root gradings
items.statement:
Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define
$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$
the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then $U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta]$, where $U_q^+[\beta]=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+$ and $U_q^-[\beta]=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-$; $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$; and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$ one has $K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x$ (the weight rule), so $U_q^0$ acts on each homogeneous component by the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; thus $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra of the free abelian group $P^{\vee}$. Similarly $U_q^\pm$ is spanned by the monomials in the $E_i$ (respectively $F_i$), so that $U_q^{\ge0}:=U_q^0U_q^+$ and $U_q^{\le0}:=U_q^-U_q^0$ span the nonnegative and nonpositive parts. Nothing in this definition asserts that these spanning families are independent or that the natural maps are injective; that is [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].
items.strategy: Work in the root-lattice grading supplied by the Drinfeld–Jimbo presentation. Every monomial in E_i has degree in Q_+, every monomial in F_i has degree in -Q_+, and every monomial in K_h has degree zero; finite sums and the direct grading give the claimed intersections and direct sums. The toral weight rule follows on each generator and then on words by multiplicativity. Define the group algebra locally as finite sums of symbols X_h with X_hX_h′=X_{h+h′}; the map X_h↦K_h is onto U_q^0 by the K relations and generation, so the first isomorphism theorem identifies U_q^0 with a quotient by its kernel. The E/F word spans and Borel product spans follow from the definitions. No linear independence or injectivity of the generating spans is asserted, and no choice principle is used.

items.title: A nonsingular principal minor of the symmetrized Cartan matrix of size the rank
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $B=(b_{ij})$ be a real symmetric $n\times n$ matrix of rank $r$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, write $B_J=(b_{ij})_{i,j\in J}$ for its principal submatrix. Use the convention that the empty matrix has determinant $1$ and is invertible. There is a subset $J$ with $|J|=r$ for which $B_J$ is nonsingular.

If in addition $A$ is a real $n\times n$ matrix and $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ has $d_i>0$ with $B=DA$, then for the same $J$,

$$\det B_J=\Bigl(\prod_{i\in J}d_i\Bigr)\det A_J.$$

Thus $A_J$ is also nonsingular and has size $r$, and $|\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J|=n-r$. In particular, if $A$ is symmetrizable and has corank one, then $B=DA$ has corank one and the conclusion gives a nonsingular $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ principal submatrix.
items.strategy: Set det of the empty matrix to 1 and handle rank zero separately. For positive rank, a nonzero real symmetric matrix has either a nonzero diagonal entry or a nonzero two-by-two principal determinant. Choose a maximal principal index set J with det(B_J) nonzero. The Schur-complement determinant formula shows that adjoining one index gives zero diagonal residual; adjoining two gives a symmetric two-by-two residual with zero diagonal and determinant minus a square, so its off-diagonal is also zero. Thus the full residual vanishes and B factors through a |J|-dimensional space: its rank is at most |J|. Its nonzero |J|-rowed principal minor makes the rank at least |J|, proving |J|=rank(B). If B=DA with D positive diagonal, B_J=D_J A_J and determinant multiplicativity gives det(B_J)=(prod_{i in J} d_i)det(A_J), so A_J is nonsingular. A corank-one symmetrizable matrix has the corresponding n-1 block. The cited Gabber–Kac example is the positive-semidefinite corank-one case; this local principal-minor proof does not require semidefiniteness. No choice principle is used; all selections are from finite families.

items.title: The formal quantum shuffle Borel and its Cartan crossed product
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), $n=|I|$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}A$. Choose $J\subseteq I$ with $|J|=r$ and $\det(A_J)\ne0$, as supplied by [[lem-nonsingular-principal-minor-of-the-symmetrized-cartan-matrix]]. Work over $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ with $q=e^{\hbar}$ and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$.

(a) **Word space and shuffle product.** Let $V=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb C v_i$ with $\deg v_i=\epsilon_i\in\mathbb N^I$. Set $\mathrm{Sh}(V)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}V^{\otimes k}\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ and denote $z_1\otimes\cdots\otimes z_k$ by $[z_1|\cdots|z_k]$. For homogeneous letters, define

$$[z_1|\cdots|z_k]\,[z_{k+1}|\cdots|z_{k+l}]=\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma_{k,l}}q^{-\sum_{i<j,\,\sigma(i)>\sigma(j)}\langle\deg z_i,\deg z_j\rangle}[z_{\sigma(1)}|\cdots|z_{\sigma(k+l)}],\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij}.$$

This product is associative and makes $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$ an $\mathbb N^I$-graded algebra; every color-degree component is a finite free $R$-module. Write $\langle V\rangle$ for the subalgebra generated by the one-letter words $[v_i]$.

(b) **Cartan derivations and crossed products.** Define $R$-linear derivations on letters by $h_i^V(v_j)=a_{ij}v_j$ and $D_j^V(v_i)=\delta_{ij}v_i$ for $j\in I\setminus J$, and extend them to words by summing their action over positions. They extend as commuting derivations of $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$ and preserve $\langle V\rangle$. Let $\mathcal C$ consist of $n$ commuting symbols $H_i$ corresponding to $h_i^V$ and $n-r$ commuting symbols $D_j$ corresponding to $D_j^V$. Put $A_C:=\varprojlim_N R[\mathcal C]/\hbar^N R[\mathcal C]\cong\mathbb C[\mathcal C]\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, so each coefficient of $\hbar^m$ is a finite Cartan polynomial. The Cartan crossed-product modules are

$$\mathcal V:=\langle V\rangle\otimes_R A_C,\qquad \mathcal S:=\mathrm{Sh}(V)\otimes_R A_C.$$

The Cartan coefficient algebra $A_C$ is $\hbar$-adically complete; no algebraic-freeness claim is made for the crossed products. Their products extend the products of the two factors and obey $X_s x-xX_s=\delta_s(x)$ for the corresponding derivation $\delta_s$. Equivalently, for multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$,

$$ (xX^\alpha)(yX^\beta)=\sum_{0\le t\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{t}x\,\delta^t(y)X^{\alpha+\beta-t},$$

where $\binom{\alpha}{t}=\prod_s\binom{\alpha_s}{t_s}$ and $\delta^t=\prod_s\delta_s^{t_s}$. The $r$ coroot directions indexed by $J$ are linearly independent because $A_J$ is nonsingular, and the remaining $n-r$ directions supplement the minimal realization of dimension $2n-r$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]]); the number of Cartan symbols is $n+(n-r)=2n-r$.

(c) **$\hbar$-adic Hopf structure and conditional Serre map.** In the commutative formal Cartan factor, define $\exp(\hbar Z)=\sum_{m\ge0}\hbar^m Z^m/m!$ for each Cartan polynomial $Z$; every coefficient is a finite polynomial, so this is an element of $A_C$. Write $\widehat\otimes_R$ for the $\hbar$-adically completed tensor product. These formulas make $\mathcal S$ a topological Hopf $R$-algebra: $\Delta:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S\widehat\otimes_R\mathcal S$ and $\varepsilon:\mathcal S\to R$ are continuous algebra maps, $\Delta$ is coassociative with both counit identities, and the continuous antipode satisfies both convolution-inverse equations.

$$\Delta_{\mathcal S}(X_s)=X_s\otimes1+1\otimes X_s,\qquad \Delta_{\mathcal S}([v_{i_1}|\cdots|v_{i_m}])=\sum_{k=0}^{m}[v_{i_1}|\cdots|v_{i_k}]\otimes\exp\!\Bigl(\hbar\sum_{t\le k}d_{i_t}H_{i_t}\Bigr)[v_{i_{k+1}}|\cdots|v_{i_m}].$$

The counit sends every nonempty word and every $X_s$ to $0$ and sends $1$ to $1$. The antipode is the common convolution inverse constructed recursively in word length and Cartan-polynomial degree. The same structure maps make $\mathcal V$ a topological Hopf subalgebra.

Let $E_R:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}Re_i$ and $T_R(E_R):=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}E_R^{\otimes_R k}$ be its tensor algebra with concatenation; every assignment of the $e_i$ to a unital $R$-algebra extends uniquely by wordwise multiplication. Let $U_{\hbar}\mathfrak n^+$ be the quotient of $T_R(E_R)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by

$$\sum_{s=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^s\binom{1-a_{ij}}{s}_{q_i}e_i^{1-a_{ij}-s}e_je_i^s=0\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the symmetric Gaussian coefficients are evaluated at $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$. Let $U_{\hbar}\mathfrak b^+$ be the crossed product of this quotient with the commuting Cartan symbols $H_i,D_j$, using the multiplication rule of part (b) for the induced derivations and acting by $[H_i,e_j]=a_{ij}e_j$ and $[D_j,e_i]=\delta_{ij}e_i$. If the quantum Serre sums vanish in $\langle V\rangle$, then $H_i\mapsto h_i^V$, $D_j\mapsto D_j^V$, and $e_i\mapsto[v_i]$ define an algebra homomorphism $p_{\hbar}:U_{\hbar}\mathfrak b^+\to\mathcal V$. This definition makes no assertion that the Serre-vanishing condition holds or that $p_{\hbar}$ is injective. All formal exponentials and completed tensor products are interpreted $\hbar$-adically; no infinite sum is multiplied outside the completion.
items.strategy: Prove shuffle associativity by three-block shuffles and the Cartan crossed product by the finite Ore formula. Identify the Cartan coefficient algebra as the h-adic completion of the polynomial ring, with finite polynomial coefficients at every h-order. Verify coproduct multiplicativity by cutting a global shuffle and matching its cross-inversion scalar with Cartan commutation; verify the crossed relations, coassociativity, counit algebra map and counit laws. Construct left and right convolution inverses recursively on word length and Cartan degree, then prove anti-multiplicativity by convolution uniqueness. Define the formal Serre quotient and its Cartan crossed product locally; state the map into the shuffle Borel only under the explicit Serre-vanishing condition. The coproduct and antipode verifications are local; no later Serre lemma or embedding theorem is used. The source wording is corrected to the completed coefficient module with no algebraic-freeness claim, and the Cartan count is n+(n-r)=2n-r.

items.title: The quantum Serre sums vanish in the shuffle algebra, and the opposite Serre ideal annihilates the shuffle half
items.statement:
Let $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$, $\langle V\rangle$ and $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$ be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]].

(i) In $\langle V\rangle\subseteq\mathrm{Sh}(V)$ the Serre sums vanish: for all $i\ne j$,
$$\sum_{s=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^s\binom{1-a_{ij}}{s}_{q_i}[v_i]^{*(1-a_{ij}-s)}*[v_j]*[v_i]^{*s}=0,$$
where $*$ is the shuffle product of [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]].

(ii) Let $V^*=\bigoplus_i\mathbb C\xi_i$ be the dual space with $\langle\xi_i,v_j\rangle=d_i^{-1}\delta_{ij}$, let $T(V^*)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(V^*)^{\otimes k}\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ be the tensor algebra on $V^*$ with concatenation product, graded by $\deg\xi_i=-\epsilon_i$, and let $\Delta:T(V^*)\to T(V^*)\otimes_R T(V^*)$ be the braided coproduct with $\Delta(\xi_i)=\xi_i\otimes1+1\otimes\xi_i$, the target carrying the braided product $(u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv'$. Let $J_-\trianglelefteq T(V^*)$ be the two-sided ideal generated by the negative Serre elements $\sum_{s=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^s\binom{1-a_{ij}}{s}_{q_i}\xi_i^{1-a_{ij}-s}\xi_j\xi_i^s$, $i\ne j$. Let
$$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{Sh}(V)\times T(V^*)}:\mathrm{Sh}(V)\times T(V^*)\to\mathbb C((\hbar)),\qquad \langle[v_{i_1}|\cdots|v_{i_k}],\xi_{j_1}\cdots\xi_{j_l}\rangle=\delta_{kl}\,\hbar^{-k}\prod_{t=1}^{k}\langle v_{i_t},\xi_{j_t}\rangle,$$
be the wordwise pairing, extended bilinearly from the tensor-word bases. Then $J_-$ annihilates the shuffle half $\langle V\rangle$:
$$\langle x,y\rangle=0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\langle V\rangle,\ y\in J_-,$$
equivalently the wordwise pairing descends to a bilinear pairing $\langle V\rangle\times\bigl(T(V^*)/J_-\bigr)\to\mathbb C((\hbar))$. The twisted product on $T(V^*)\otimes_R T(V^*)$ is used only in the definition of the braided coproduct, and no claim is made about the radical of the pairing on all of $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$ (see the note after the proof).
items.strategy: Prove positive Serre vanishing by expanding a fixed word coefficient in the three-block quantum shuffle. The coefficient factors into two finite Gaussian sums; the q-binomial product expansion makes one factor vanish at an endpoint for every word. items.title: An augmented coideal ideal of an enveloping algebra is generated by its primitive part
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathfrak l$ be a Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field $k$, and equip $U\mathfrak l$ with its standard coproduct $\Delta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. If $J\trianglelefteq U\mathfrak l$ is a two-sided ideal with $\Delta(J)\subseteq J\otimes U\mathfrak l+U\mathfrak l\otimes J$ and $J\subseteq\ker\varepsilon$, then $\mathfrak j:=J\cap\mathfrak l$ is a Lie ideal and $J=(U\mathfrak l)\mathfrak j=\mathfrak j(U\mathfrak l)$. Thus $J$ is uniquely determined by $\mathfrak j$ among ideals satisfying both conditions.
items.strategy: Use AC to choose and well-order a basis of $\mathfrak l$ and apply the general PBW theorem. The standard coproduct is filtered and induces the primitive coproduct on $S\mathfrak l$. The augmentation hypothesis gives $(\operatorname{gr}J)_0=0$ and $(\operatorname{gr}J)_1=J\cap\mathfrak l$. The associated graded ideal is a coideal; induction on degree, followed by $S(\mathfrak l)\to S(\mathfrak l/\mathfrak j)$ and the fact that characteristic-zero symmetric algebras have no primitive homogeneous elements above degree one, shows $\operatorname{gr}J$ is the ideal generated by $\mathfrak j$. PBW then lifts this equality to $J=U\mathfrak j=\mathfrak jU$. AC also supplies the compatible vector-space splittings used to pass the coideal containment to the associated graded. The source's printed statement omits $\varepsilon(J)=0$; the local item includes it because $J=U\mathfrak l$ is a counterexample otherwise.

items.title: The opposite Borels of a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra are root-degreewise dual Lie bialgebras
items.statement: Let $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be a finite symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix over $\mathbb C$, with positive symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)$ and rank $r$. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g(A)$ have minimal Cartan realization $\mathfrak h$, triangular decomposition $\mathfrak n^-\oplus\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$, and Borels $\mathfrak b^\pm=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^\pm$. Normalize the invariant form by $(h_i|h)=\alpha_i(h)/d_i$ and $(e_i|f_j)=\delta_{ij}/d_i$. (i) The form induces a canonical degreewise perfect vector-space pairing on $U(\mathfrak n^+)$ and $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ by PBW symmetrization; their root-degree pieces are finite-dimensional, so $U(\mathfrak n^-)\cong (U(\mathfrak n^+))^{\mathrm{gr}\prime}$ and conversely. This is not a Hopf pairing for the standard primitive coproducts. (ii) If $J\subset I$ indexes a nonsingular principal block $A_J$ of size $r$, choose coordinates $D_j$ for $j\notin J$ with $\alpha_i(D_j)=\delta_{ij}$. In $\mathfrak d=\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak h$ with form $B_{\mathfrak d}((x,a),(y,b))=(x|y)-(a|b)$, the maps $h+x_+\mapsto(h+x_+,h)$ and $h+x_-\mapsto(h+x_-,-h)$ embed the Borels as complementary isotropic subalgebras. Thus they form a locally finite root-graded Manin triple with cross pairing $2(h|h')+(x_+|x_-)$; its transpose brackets give dual Lie bialgebra structures whose cobrackets vanish on $\mathfrak h$.
items.strategy: The invariant form gives perfect pairings of opposite root spaces. Use the finite simple-generator Serre presentations for finite root-degree pieces, a countably ordered bracket-word basis for the halves, and PBW symmetrization to transport the symmetrized root-space pairing to their enveloping algebras. Use the nonsingular principal block to choose the complementary Cartan coordinates. The root-graded Manin double is $\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak h$ with complementary isotropic Borel images; the finite-piece Manin-triple theorem gives the dual Lie bialgebra structures. The enveloping-algebra pairing is a vector-space pairing and is not extended by primitive-coproduct Hopf adjunction.

items.title: The formal quantum Serre half embeds in the shuffle algebra and is degreewise free
items.statement:
Let $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\mathcal V$, $\langle V\rangle$, and $p_\hbar:U_\hbar\mathfrak b^+\to\mathcal V$ be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], with $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ and $q=e^\hbar$, and let $U\mathfrak n^+$ be the positive half of the Kac–Moody algebra. Assume AC; it is used only to apply the two-sided coideal lemma in step 2.1. For an indeterminate $q'$, let $U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+$ be the algebra over $\mathbb C(q')$ with the same generators and positive quantum Serre relations, with $q_i'=q'^{d_i}$. Then:

(i) The composite $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\to U_\hbar\mathfrak b^+\xrightarrow{p_\hbar}\mathcal V$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras onto $\langle V\rangle$. In particular, $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$ is a free $R$-module and each root-graded component $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]$ is a finite-rank free $R$-module.

(ii) The classical limit is the classical half: $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+/\hbar U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\cong U\mathfrak n^+$ as $\mathbb N^I$-graded algebras, by $e_i\mapsto\bar e_i$.

(iii) For every $\alpha\in Q_+$,
$$\operatorname{rank}_{R}U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(q')}U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+[\alpha].$$
items.strategy: Use the proved positive shuffle-vanishing clause to define the conditional algebra map and reduce it to the classical Borel. Prove the classical map is Hopf on primitive generators, apply the AC-dependent coideal lemma, and use degreewise Lie-bialgebra duality of opposite Borels to kill the primitive kernel. For each root degree, compare the finite free shuffle target with the classical reduction using the PID structure theorem to eliminate torsion. Transfer finite presentation ranks to the generic parameter through q prime maps to e^h and equality of matrix-minor ranks. The proof makes no quantum Hopf claim for p_h and does not use the Serre supplier radical clause.

items.title: Generic quantum Serre halves have classical PBW ranks and a nondegenerate Hopf pairing
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $q=e^{\hbar}$ and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$, and let $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$, $T(V^*)$ and the Serre ideal $J_-$ be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]; write $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-:=T(V^*)/J_-$. Assume the axiom of choice AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); it enters only through [[thm-the-formal-quantum-serre-half-embeds-in-the-quantum-shuffle-algebra-and-is-degreewise-free]] in part (i). Let $q'$ be an indeterminate and let $U_{q'}\mathfrak n^{\pm}$ be the $\mathbb C(q')$-algebras with generators $e_i'$ (respectively $f_i'$), $i\in I$, and the quantum Serre relations
$$\sum_{s=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^s\binom{1-a_{ij}}{s}_{q_i'}e_i'^{1-a_{ij}-s}e_j'e_i'^s=0\qquad(i\ne j),$$
respectively their negative analogues, where $q_i'=q'^{d_i}$.

(i) **Generic PBW ranks.** For every $\alpha\in Q_+$,
$$\operatorname{rank}_R U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(q')}U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+[\alpha],$$
and the same three numbers equal $\operatorname{rank}_R U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-[-\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U\mathfrak n^-[-\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(q')}U_{q'}\mathfrak n^-[-\alpha]$. In particular every $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is a finite free $R$-module of the classical PBW rank, and every family of homogeneous lifts of a $\mathbb C$-basis of $U\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]$ (respectively of $U\mathfrak n^-[-\alpha]$) is an $R$-basis of the corresponding formal component.

(ii) **Nondegenerate pairing.** The wordwise pairing of [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]](ii) descends to a $\mathbb C((\hbar))$-valued pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\times U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-\to\mathbb C((\hbar))$, and this pairing is nondegenerate: its left and right annihilators are zero. It satisfies the two adjunction rules
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad \langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle ,$$
with the cut coproduct on the first argument and the braided coproduct of $T(V^*)$ on the second, understood on the realizing models: for $y\in U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$ and any representative $\tilde y\in T(V^*)$ the value $\sum\langle x,(\tilde y)_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',(\tilde y)_{(2)}\rangle$ is independent of the representative and equals $\langle xx',y\rangle$. The rescaled pairing normalized to $\langle e_i,f_{i'}\rangle=\hbar^{1-d_i}\delta_{ii'}$ differs from it by unit factors and is nondegenerate as well; equivalently, the $\mathbb C(q')$-bilinear pairing $U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+\times U_{q'}\mathfrak n^-\to\mathbb C(q')$ given by the same word formula and the substitution $q'=e^{\hbar}$ is nondegenerate, so that the generic halves are graded dual to one another.
items.strategy:
This is Enriquez's Theorem 1.2, Corollaries 1.2-1.3 and the generic transfer of §2.4. (i) By [[thm-the-formal-quantum-serre-half-embeds-in-the-quantum-shuffle-algebra-and-is-degreewise-free]] each $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is a free $\mathbb C[[\hbar]]$-module of rank $\dim U\mathfrak n^\pm[\alpha]$, and its generic fibre $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^\pm[\pm\alpha]\otimes_{\mathbb C[[\hbar]]}\mathbb \mathbb C((\hbar))$ has the same dimension over $\mathbb \mathbb C((\hbar))$; the identification $q'=e^{\hbar}$ (formally, inverting $\hbar$) identifies that fibre with $U_{q'}\mathfrak n^\pm[\pm\alpha]\otimes_{\mathbb C(q')}\mathbb \mathbb C((\hbar))$, and faithful scalar extension (a $\mathbb C(q')$-basis remains a basis after extending scalars to the field of fractions $\operatorname{Frac}\mathbb \mathbb C[[\hbar]]$, by faithful scalar extension [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]) gives (i); this is the 'finite-matrix reflection of independence' the source performs in Corollary 1.2 and §2.4.

(ii) Follow §2.2. Introduce $V^*$ with dual basis and the tensor algebra $T(V^*)$ with its braided Hopf structure, and the braided pairing $\langle[z_1|\cdots|z_k],\xi_{j_1}\cdots\xi_{j_l}\rangle=\delta_{kl}\hbar^{-k}\prod_t\langle z_t,\xi_{j_t}\rangle$, whose restriction to $V^{\otimes k}\times(V^*)^{\otimes k}$ is the natural nondegenerate pairing of dual tensor powers, so that the annihilator of $T(V^*)$ in $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$ is zero. By [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]](ii) the ideal defining $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$ lies in the radical, so the pairing descends to $\mathrm{Sh}(V)\times U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$; by [[thm-the-formal-quantum-serre-half-embeds-in-the-quantum-shuffle-algebra-and-is-degreewise-free]] $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$ is a subalgebra of $\mathrm{Sh}(V)$, so the pairing restricts to $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\times U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$. Its annihilator on each side is zero: if $y\in U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$ is annihilated, then in particular it pairs trivially with $T(V^*)$'s... with all of $\mathrm{Sh}(V)\supseteq U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$; using the descending identification and the nondegeneracy of the tensor-word pairing one gets $y=0$ (the source argues with the annihilator of $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^-$ in $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$ and Lemma 2.11). Since the pairing is graded and the graded components of the two halves have equal $\mathbb C[[\hbar]]$-ranks by part (i) (isomorphic by the pairing), nondegeneracy on the whole follows from nondegeneracy of each graded component; the components are finite-dimensional over $\mathbb \mathbb C((\hbar))$ and are handled by the finite-dimensional duality $M\times M^*\to k$, with bases transported by [[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]]. The generic statement is the scalar extension of §2.4.

items.title: The generic quantum halves form a Drinfeld-Jimbo crossed double
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group, let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the $F_i$, the $K_h$ and the $E_i$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

(a) **The crossed double presented by cross-relations.** Let $W:=U_q^-\oplus U_q^0\oplus U_q^+$ be the direct sum of the three underlying vector spaces, let $T(W)$ be its tensor algebra with unit $1_{T(W)}$ (the empty word), and let $J\subseteq T(W)$ be the two-sided ideal generated by the following elements:

$$u\otimes v-uv\qquad(u,v\ \text{in one common factor }U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+),$$
$$1_{U_q^-}-1_{T(W)},\qquad 1_{U_q^0}-1_{T(W)},\qquad 1_{U_q^+}-1_{T(W)},$$
$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I),$$
$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I),$$

where in the last three lines the symbols denote the corresponding elements of $W$. Then $D:=T(W)/J$ is an associative unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra, and the inclusions of the three factors define unital algebra homomorphisms $\iota_-:U_q^-\to D$, $\iota_0:U_q^0\to D$, $\iota_+:U_q^+\to D$. The algebra $D$ has the following **universal property**: for every unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$ and every triple of unital algebra homomorphisms $f_-:U_q^-\to B$, $f_0:U_q^0\to B$, $f_+:U_q^+\to B$ whose images satisfy

$$\text{(b)}\quad f_0(K_h)f_\pm(x)f_0(K_h)^{-1}=q^{\pm\beta(h)}f_\pm(x)\quad(x\in U_q^\pm[\pm\beta]\ \text{homogeneous},\ h\in P^{\vee}),$$
$$\text{(c)}\quad f_+(E_i)f_-(F_j)-f_-(F_j)f_+(E_i)=\delta_{ij}\frac{f_0(K_i)-f_0(K_i^{-1})}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I),$$

there is a unique unital algebra homomorphism $F:D\to B$ with $F\circ\iota_-=f_-$, $F\circ\iota_0=f_0$, $F\circ\iota_+=f_+$. In particular $D$ is determined by this property up to a unique isomorphism.

(b) **Toral cross-relations in $D$.** For every $h\in P^{\vee}$ and every homogeneous $x\in U_q^\pm[\pm\beta]$, $\iota_0(K_h)\iota_\pm(x)\iota_0(K_h)^{-1}=q^{\pm\beta(h)}\iota_\pm(x)$; also $\iota_0(K_h)^{-1}=\iota_0(K_{-h})$.

(c) **Identification with $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.** The assignments $\psi(E_i):=\iota_+(E_i)$, $\psi(F_i):=\iota_-(F_i)$, $\psi(K_h):=\iota_0(K_h)$ extend uniquely to algebra homomorphisms $\psi:U_q(\mathfrak g)\to D$ and $\phi:D\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with $\phi(\iota_-(x_-)\iota_0(x_0)\iota_+(x_+))=x_-x_0x_+$ for all $x_-\in U_q^-$, $x_0\in U_q^0$, $x_+\in U_q^+$. They are mutually inverse, so $D\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ as $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebras and $\iota_-,\iota_0,\iota_+$ are injective.

(d) **Spanning.** Every element of $D$ is a finite sum of products $\iota_-(x_-)\iota_0(x_0)\iota_+(x_+)$; equivalently, the linear map $U_q^-\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+\to D$, $x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\mapsto\iota_-(x_-)\iota_0(x_0)\iota_+(x_+)$ is surjective.

**Scope of the claim.** Neither the injectivity of the map in (d) -- equivalently, the identification of the underlying vector space of $D$ with $U_q^-\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+$ and the freeness of this presentation as a crossed (Drinfeld) double -- nor the description of the general cross product $\iota_+(x)\iota_-(y)$ by the pairing formula of the Drinfeld double is proved here; the proof uses neither the formal shuffle model nor the Hopf pairing. Both statements are the open inputs of [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]. The construction uses no choice principle.
items.strategy: Construct $D$ as a presented algebra and record its universal property; build comparison maps in both directions from the universal properties of $T(W)$ and $U_q(\mathfrak g)$; show that they are mutually inverse on generators; then transfer the toral cross-relations and the spanning property from generators by multiplicativity and a finite rearrangement induction.

items.title: Triangular decomposition of a quantized enveloping algebra
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group, let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be the subalgebras generated by the $F_i$, the $K_h$ and the $E_i$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Let $T(W)$ be the free algebra on the symbols $E_i,F_i,K_h$ and let $\widetilde U:=T(W)/\widetilde I$, where $\widetilde I$ is generated by the toral relations $K_0-1$, $K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}$, by $K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h$, $K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h$ and by $E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ -- that is, by the defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ *without* the two quantum Serre families. Write $\widetilde U^{\pm},\widetilde U^{0}$ for the subalgebras of $\widetilde U$ generated by the $E_i$, the $F_i$ and the $K_h$, and let $I^{\pm}$ be the two-sided ideal of the free algebra $\widetilde U^{\pm}$ generated by the family $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ ($i\ne j$). Let $m:U_q^-\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the multiplication map $x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\mapsto x_-x_0x_+$.

Assume the following two inputs, neither of which is proved in this item:

**(A1) Serre-free decomposition.** $\widetilde U^{0}\cong\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$ is the group algebra of $P^{\vee}$, $\widetilde U^{\pm}$ are the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebras on the $E_i$ and the $F_i$, and the multiplication map $\widetilde U^-\otimes\widetilde U^{0}\otimes\widetilde U^+\to\widetilde U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector spaces. In particular it is injective.

**(A2) Serre ideal identity.** Let $\langle\mathrm{Serre}\rangle\subseteq\widetilde U$ be the two-sided ideal generated by both Serre families. Then, under the identification (A1),
$$\langle\mathrm{Serre}\rangle= I^-\widetilde U^{0}\widetilde U^+ +\widetilde U^- \widetilde U^{0}I^+ .$$

Then:

(i) $m:U_q^-\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector spaces.

(ii) $U_q^+\cong\widetilde U^+/I^+$ and $U_q^-\cong\widetilde U^-/I^-$, so $U_q^\pm$ is the quotient of the free algebra on the $E_i$ (respectively $F_i$) by the separate Serre relations; and $U_q^0\cong\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$ is the group algebra of $P^{\vee}$. In particular the $K_h$ are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and $K_h\ne1$ for $h\ne0$.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, $m$ restricts to an isomorphism $\bigoplus_{\beta_++\beta_-=\beta}U_q^-[-\beta_-]\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+[\beta_+]\to U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$, and the rank of $U_q^+[\alpha]$ equals the classical PBW rank $\dim_{\mathbb C}U\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]$ for every $\alpha\in Q_+$ (the same for the negative half). Consequently $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]=U_q^0$, and for $\beta\ne0$ the component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is a free $U_q^0$-module of rank $\sum_{\beta_++\beta_-=\beta}\dim U\mathfrak n^+[\beta_+]\cdot\dim U\mathfrak n^-[-\beta_-]$.

**Open obligation.** (A1) and (A2) are not established in this item. The exact missing suppliers, in dependency order, are: the triangular decomposition of the Serre-free presentation $\widetilde U$ (its proof is a rewriting/diamond argument: the reduction rules $K_hE_i\to q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h$, $K_hF_i\to q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h$, $E_iF_j\to F_jE_i+\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ have only the overlaps $KKE$, $KKF$ and $KEF$, which resolve by the q-power identity $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}q^{-\langle\alpha_j,h\rangle}=q^{\langle\alpha_i-\alpha_j,h\rangle}$), and the annihilation statement $[F_k,\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}]=[E_k,\mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}]=0$ in $\widetilde U$ (a finite q-binomial computation; it implies (A2) by absorbing the $E$- and $F$-parts of an ambient word into the ideal factor). The source prints exactly this reduction: Berkeley, Lemma 13.1.3.21 and the proof of Theorem 13.1.3.22, using the Serre-free presentation of Definition 13.1.3.12. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Reduce the triangular decomposition of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ to the Serre-free presentation, where it is the input (A1), by comparing the two kernels in the commuting square of quotient maps; the Serre ideal identity (A2) forces the two kernels to coincide.

items.title: Divided-power commutation and the simple $U_{q_i}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ string modules
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $\mathbb A$ of the $1\times1$ Cartan matrix $(2)$ with symmetrizer $(d_i)$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}v_N$, where $v_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}v_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

**Open obligation.** Part (i) (linear independence of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$) and the nonvanishing of $v_0,\dots,v_N$ and the simplicity in part (iii) use the triangular decomposition of [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], whose decision is currently escalated because its inputs (A1), (A2) are unauthored. The consuming steps below are marked. All other claims are proved locally.

items.title: Unsymmetrized parameters break the coproduct of the Serre ideal
items.statement:
The following statement is false. *For every generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and every assignment of nonzero parameters $q_i$ to the nodes, the formulas $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$ together with the toral rules $K_iE_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{a_{ij}}E_j$ define an algebra homomorphism $T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\to(T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\otimes(T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}})$; that is, the ideal generated by the Serre sums is a coideal.*

**Counterexample.** Take the Cartan matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$ of $B_2$, whose symmetrizer is $D=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, and use the unsymmetrized parameters $q_1=q_2=q$ (so $K_1E_2K_1^{-1}=q^{-1}E_2$ while $K_2E_1K_2^{-1}=q^{-2}E_1$). Then, in the free algebra modulo the toral relations, the expansion of $\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12})$ with $\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}=E_1^2E_2-[2]_qE_1E_2E_1+E_2E_1^2$ contains, besides $\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}\otimes K_1^{-2}K_2^{-1}+1\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}$, the nonzero mixed terms
$$q^{-2}(1-q)(1+q^{2})\,E_1E_2\otimes E_1K_1^{-1}K_2^{-1}\;-\;q^{-1}(1-q)(1+q^{2})\,E_2E_1\otimes E_1K_1^{-1}K_2^{-1}+(1-q)(1+q^{3})\,E_2\otimes E_1^2K_2^{-1}+\cdots$$
(the displayed coefficients are nonzero since $q$ is transcendental). The $(2,1)$-component — two $E$-letters on the left, one on the right — of $I_+\otimes T+T\otimes I_+$ is zero because every element of $I_+$ has $E$-degree at least $3$, while the mixed part has nonzero $(2,1)$-component; hence $\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12})\notin I_+\otimes T+T\otimes I_+$ and $\Delta$ does not descend. With the correct symmetrized parameters $q_1=q^{2}$, $q_2=q$ the two crossing constants agree ($q_1^{a_{12}}=q^{-2}=q_2^{a_{21}}$) and the same expansion has every mixed coefficient zero, so the defect is exactly the Cartan normalization $q_i^{a_{ij}}=q_j^{a_{ji}}$; for a nonsymmetrizable $A$ no assignment of the form $q_i=q^{d_i}$ exists at all.
items.strategy: Compute the B2 positive Serre coproduct in the toral-action Borel with q1=q2=q. Use the crossed word algebra to establish independence of the length-two words, then project to left/right word lengths (2,1). This proves that the positive Borel Serre ideal is not a coideal. The scaffold additionally claims failure in the quotient by all Drinfeld–Jimbo relations; the Borel calculation alone does not establish that extension, which remains an explicit open obligation because the mixed E_iF_j relations may change the quotient.

items.title: The quasiprimitive Serre element in type $A_2$
items.statement:
In the Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of type $A_2$ (the Cartan datum $I=\{1,2\}$, $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$, $d_1=d_2=1$, so $q_1=q_2=q$) the Serre elements
$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}=E_1^2E_2-[2]_qE_1E_2E_1+E_2E_1^2,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{12}=F_1^2F_2-[2]_qF_1F_2F_1+F_2F_1^2,\qquad [2]_q=q+q^{-1},$$
are quasiprimitive with explicit grouplike factors:
$$\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12})=\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}\otimes K_1^{-2}K_2^{-1}+1\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12},\qquad \Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12})=\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12}\otimes1+K_1^{2}K_2\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12}.$$
In particular every mixed bidegree term in the expansion of $\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^\pm_{12})$ cancels, and at $q=1$ the positive relation degenerates to the classical Serre relation $[E_1,[E_1,E_2]]=\mathrm{ad}(e_1)^2e_2=0$ of $A_2$.
items.strategy: For A2, write the three-letter positive Serre polynomial and use the toral crossing rules to enumerate the left/right choices in its coproduct. The six mixed tensor-word coefficients are, in bidegree (2,1), 1+q^{-2}-[2]_q q^{-1}, q^2-[2]_q q+1, -[2]_q+q+q^{-1}, and, in bidegree (1,2), q^{-1}+q-[2]_q, 1-[2]_q q+q^2, -[2]_q q^{-1}+q^{-2}+1; each is zero for [2]_q=q+q^{-1}. The all-left/all-right terms give the positive quasiprimitive formula. The negative formula is the A2 instance of the preceding coproduct/Serre lemma. At q=1, the polynomial Serre expression equals [e1,[e1,e2]] and vanishes by the classical A2 Serre relation; this is not an assertion that the whole Q(q)-algebra specializes.

items.title: The double-edge Serre relation for the cyclic affine type $A_1^{(1)}$
items.statement:
For the double edge $a_{12}=a_{21}=-2$ (the Cartan matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$ of the cyclic affine type $A_1^{(1)}$, with $d_1=d_2=1$) the quantum Serre relation has $m=1-a_{12}=3$:
$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}=E_1^3E_2-[3]_qE_1^2E_2E_1+[3]_qE_1E_2E_1^2-E_2E_1^3,\qquad [3]_q=q^{2}+1+q^{-2},$$
and it is quasiprimitive: $\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12})=\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}\otimes K_1^{-3}K_2^{-1}+1\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^+_{12}$, while $\Delta(\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12})=\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12}\otimes1+K_1^{3}K_2\otimes\mathrm{Serre}^-_{12}$. The coefficients satisfy the alternating Gaussian identity $\sum_{r=0}^{3}(-1)^{r}q^{2r}\binom{3}{r}_q=0$ of [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]], and at $q=1$ the positive relation becomes the cubic classical Serre relation $\mathrm{ad}(e_1)^3e_2=0$ of the affine type $A_1^{(1)}$ (the $e=2$ double-edge case).
items.strategy: For A1^(1), enumerate the left/right choices in each four-letter positive Serre word. The toral crossing factor for a left E_i before a right E_j is q^{-2} if i=j and q^2 if i!=j. Group the mixed terms into four words in each bidegree (3,1), (2,2), and (1,3); the item gives every coefficient. Substitution [3]_q=q^2+1+q^{-2} makes all twelve vanish, with the (1,3) endpoint coefficient also the N=3 alternating Gaussian identity. The extreme splits give the two positive terms. The negative formula is the specialization of the preceding general toral-action Borel lemma. At q=1 the polynomial Serre expression is ad(e1)^3 e2 and vanishes by the classical Serre presentation; this does not assert that the whole Q(q)-algebra specializes.
